macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum mostly held up, while broader crypto market was flat to slightly lower
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $65,000 to $65,760 over the last 24 hours, while Ethereum rose about 1.6% to 1.7% and several altcoins also posted modest gains. Other reports said the overall crypto market cap slipped about 1% to 1.2% as traders weighed macro pressure from oil, rates, and risk sentiment.

items.title: Bitcoin briefly dropped below $64,000 amid volatility and liquidations
items.summary: Market coverage reported Bitcoin falling below $64,000 intraday, with one report citing about $87 million in Bitcoin liquidations and $312 million across the broader crypto market. The move was tied to renewed Iran-related geopolitical tension and wider market weakness.

items.title: Coinbase restored prediction markets trading after a temporary outage
items.summary: Reuters reported that Coinbase said it restored prediction markets trading on its platform after users were temporarily unable to place trades. The interruption was short-lived, but it was a notable operational issue for a major exchange.

items.title: Swift launched a blockchain-based shared ledger with 16 banks
items.summary: Swift said it launched a blockchain-based shared ledger with an initial group of 16 banks, including Citi and HSBC, to support round-the-clock payments. The move is part of a broader push to modernize payments and compete with stablecoin infrastructure.

items.title: Sen. Wyden urged Senate leaders to preserve blockchain developer protections in crypto legislation
items.summary: The Block reported that Sen. Wyden is pushing Senate leaders to keep contested blockchain developer protections in a broader crypto bill. The debate centers on how much legal protection developers should receive as Congress works on market-structure legislation.

items.title: European Commission reportedly considering expanding MiCA to cover tokenization and non-EU stablecoin issuers
items.summary: The Block reported that the European Commission is looking to expand MiCA to address tokenization and stablecoin issuers outside the EU. If pursued, the change would broaden the regulatory perimeter around digital assets in Europe.

items.title: Gate said recent security incident exposed customer external information
items.summary: Odaily reported that Gate responded to a recent security event by saying customer external information had leaked and that it was tracing fund flows. The incident adds to ongoing exchange-security concerns in the sector.

items.title: Binance Wallet added Plume yield vault access to Invesco and Bitwise funds
items.summary: The Block reported that Binance Wallet expanded support for Plume's yield vault offering, giving users access to products linked to Invesco and Bitwise funds. The development points to continued growth in tokenized yield and wallet-integrated investment products.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent inside ChatGPT designed to execute tasks across different apps and files, expanding its push into professional AI tools. The release intensifies competition in enterprise automation with Anthropic and Meta.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-Live voice models for real-time conversation
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The company says the capability is aimed at more natural live conversations and use cases such as translation.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to its Muse Spark AI model and an upgraded version, signaling a more direct challenge to paid AI model offerings from Anthropic and OpenAI. The move expands Meta’s presence in the commercial model market.

items.title: Grok 4.5 debuts as xAI targets coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: xAI launched Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model yet and positioning it for coding and agentic workflows. The release is part of the rapid competition among frontier model developers.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body meant to keep the company aligned with its public mission. The move highlights governance and safety as major themes in AI company strategy.

items.title: Trump administration lifts restrictions on Anthropic Claude models
items.summary: The Trump administration lifted restrictions on Anthropic’s latest Claude versions after a cybersecurity-related ban. The reversal allows broader deployment of Anthropic’s newest models.

items.title: OpenAI faces new sanctions motion in copyright case
items.summary: News publishers filed a new motion alleging OpenAI hid tools and datasets that could identify copyrighted journalism in ChatGPT outputs. The filing escalates the company’s ongoing copyright litigation.

items.title: Anthropic $1.5 billion copyright settlement approved
items.summary: A federal judge approved a $1.5 billion settlement requiring Anthropic to pay thousands of authors for training Claude on pirated books. The decision is one of the largest legal resolutions yet in AI copyright disputes.

items.title: Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 draws attention with a massive open-weight model
items.summary: Chinese startup Moonshot AI released Kimi K3, a new model that it says has 2.8 trillion total parameters and may rival leading U.S. systems at lower cost. The release adds to the momentum behind large open-weight models from China.

items.title: Thinking Machines unveils Inkling as its first general-purpose model
items.summary: Thinking Machines introduced Inkling, an open-weight model that users can download and customize. It is the startup’s first general-purpose model release and another sign of growing competition in open AI systems.

items.title: Meta plans in-house AI chip production
items.summary: Reuters reported that Meta plans to start manufacturing an AI chip in September as part of a broader effort to expand computing capacity. The internal memo points to continued heavy infrastructure spending across the AI industry.

items.title: Micron announces more than $250 billion U.S. investment
items.summary: Micron said it will invest more than $250 billion in the United States through 2035, citing surging demand for memory chips in the AI era. The announcement underscores how AI demand continues to drive semiconductor investment.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Microsoft’s Xbox division faces major layoffs and studio changes
items.summary: Reports indicate Microsoft cut jobs across multiple Xbox teams, including ZeniMax and other studios, as part of a broader restructuring of its gaming business. Several reports also say some studios are being sold or spun out as Xbox refocuses on fewer, larger franchises.

items.title: IO Interactive to close one studio after Xbox funding was pulled
items.summary: IO Interactive, the developer behind Hitman and 007: First Light, is closing one of its studios and laying off staff after Xbox reportedly withdrew funding for a project. The studio says its next franchise project, Project Fantasy, will still move forward.

items.title: Nintendo says it will keep selling the original Switch outside Europe
items.summary: Nintendo has clarified that it will continue selling the original Switch in markets outside Europe. The decision comes as speculation grows about how long the aging console will remain on sale.

items.title: Capcom moves up Onimusha: Way of the Sword release date
items.summary: Capcom has reportedly advanced the launch of Onimusha: Way of the Sword to September 4 from the previously planned September 25 release date. The change gives the long-awaited action game an earlier launch window.

items.title: Nintendo confirms Mario Kart Tour will shut down in September
items.summary: Nintendo has announced that Mario Kart Tour will be discontinued after seven years of service. The company does not plan to offer an offline version after shutdown.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced launches with strong Steam numbers
items.summary: The new Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced release has drawn a large player peak on Steam, with reports saying it reached around 100,000 concurrent players. That would make it the franchise’s strongest Steam launch to date.

items.title: Pokémon Go marks its 10th anniversary with live event coverage
items.summary: Niantic’s Pokémon Go held a livestream tied to the game’s 10th anniversary, with announcements and event details unfolding during the broadcast. The event centered on celebrations and new in-game surprises.

items.title: Fortnite adds an American Dad crossover bundle
items.summary: Epic Games released a new American Dad-themed crossover bundle in Fortnite’s item shop. The launch drew fan backlash because the bundle reportedly excludes Roger.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 ports are now available on PS4 and PS5
items.summary: IGN reports that Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 have been released on PS4 and PS5. The ports are now available, though the pricing has been described as high.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 is getting a standalone launcher
items.summary: According to VGTimes, Black Ops 6 will become a standalone title with its own dedicated launcher instead of remaining inside the unified Call of Duty HQ hub. The change is scheduled to take effect on July 7.
